page: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v6 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance belonging to the Dldsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache. This instance is configured with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It includes 5669 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the D96lds_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core performance. The Geekbench multi-core score of 21105.0 and PassMark CPU score of 86003.68 both rank in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 495.7 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput achieved a top-tier result of 110.74 GB/sec. The processor's support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) assists in compute-heavy tasks, as reflected in the strong PassMark CPU extended instructions score of 101312.09. For LLM inference, the instance processed 252.33 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a medium 7B model and 35.02 tokens/sec on a large 70B model.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the D96lds_v6 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive databases or massive in-memory datasets. However, this low memory-to-CPU ratio provides a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The inclusion of 5669 GB of local storage makes it appropriate for applications requiring substantial local scratch space. This instance is configured for multi-threaded software compilation, image processing, web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
